title: SLO-driven fractional capacity pricing playbook
author: Liam Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a new pricing and packaging offering: SLO-driven fractional capacity bundles. The objective is to let customers purchase fine-grained capacity commitments (fractional GPU / shard equivalents) that are priced and SLA'd based on declared latency and throughput SLOs. The model aims to bridge the gap between per-token usage pricing and large reserved capacity contracts by offering a predictable cost ladder tied to operational SLOs and automatic fallback rules.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Provide a predictable, lower-friction alternative to multi-month Dedicated contracts for teams that need capacity predictability tied to latency SLOs.
  - Increase conversion from self-serve to committed revenue by offering smaller commit sizes and SLO-backed discounts.
  - Expose clear levers (frac-capacity size, SLO target, burst window) that map directly to unit costs and throttling behavior.
- Non-goals:
  - Replace Dedicated annual contracts for very large enterprises.
  - Support every legacy billing model immediately; this playbook focuses on the fractional-capacity product and migration story.

Target customers:
- Mid-market product teams with stable but moderate traffic (1k-50k requests/day) who need latency guarantees but not full reserved racks.
- Platform teams prototyping SLO-aligned internal chargeback models.
- ML-driven SaaS apps that want predictable per-session economics for conversational features.

Background and motivation:
- Current options: Hosted per-token pricing (high variance) and Dedicated reserved capacity (high commitment). Customers repeatedly ask for an intermediate product that reduces cost variance without needing large commits.
- Observability and routing capabilities (our smart routing, fallbacks, and prefix-caching) make it feasible to offer fractional guarantees while preserving global availability with graceful degradation.

Product offering (high level):
- SKU: frac-capacity-{unit} (unit = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 of a session-equivalent shard). Each SKU pairs with an SLO profile (e.g., p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms) and a burst window (requests/min).
- Bundles: customers pick a bundle of N units for a billing period (monthly, quarterly) and declare an SLO profile. The system reserves proportional scheduling capacity and provides a discount vs on-demand per-token pricing.
- Fallback policies: if capacity is saturated, requests are subject to automatic fallback rules: lower-cost model variant, queued low-priority lane, or best-effort on-demand routing. These fallbacks are governed by the purchase’s fallthrough policy selected at purchase time (conservative / balanced / aggressive).

Technical requirements (summary):
1) Capacity accounting: track fractional allocations per tenant across GPU pools. Implementation notes: use the existing capacity ledger with a new fractional shard abstraction.
2) SLO enforcement: integrate with routing policy to prefer frac-capacity pool for qualifying requests and measure p95/p99 at the token and request level.
3) Billing & metering: create a monthly metering record for committed units vs consumed units, apply discounts and overage rules.
4) Telemetry: surface per-customer SLO compliance, fallback counts, and cost delta vs on-demand in Console.
5) Compatibility: support Hosted and Dedicated (Dedicated maps fractional units to dedicated pool partitions; Hosted maps to shared fractional tenancy).

Pricing & discount model (examples):
- Base on-demand rate (example): $0.0008 / token (reference).
- Fractional bundles: pricing is a function of unit size, SLO tier, and term commitment. Example table (displayed as ASCII table):
  | Bundle unit | SLO tier | Term | Discount vs on-demand | Effective unit price (example) |
  |-------------|----------|------|----------------------|-------------------------------|
  | 0.1         | p95-200ms| monthly | 12%                 | $0.000704 / token             |
  | 0.25        | p95-200ms| monthly | 18%                 | $0.000656 / token             |
  | 0.5         | p99-500ms| quarterly | 25%               | $0.0006 / token               |
  | 1.0         | p99-250ms| annual | 38%                 | $0.000496 / token             |
Notes on pricing: discounts increase with larger fractional units, tighter terms, and willingness to accept higher fallthrough aggression. The pricing engine will parameterize by observed utilization and historical fallback cost to keep revenue neutral during initial rollout.

SLO mapping and enforcement details:
- SLOs are expressed as request-level latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) and optional throughput floor (rps).
- Enforcement is conservative: routing prioritizes SLO-compliant pools but will not preempt other high-importance tenants; instead it routes to configured fallbacks once queue depth or expected latency exceeds thresholds.
- Violations: if monthly SLO compliance drops below contracted coverage (e.g., 99.9% of requests within declared p95), customers receive a credit formula (see Billing section).

Billing, credits and overage rules:
1) Committed charge: monthly invoice line for purchased units.
2) Consumption reconciliation: measured consumed tokens routed via fraction pool are billed at discounted rate up to committed units.
3) Overage: consumption beyond committed units is billed at a pre-agreed overage rate (e.g., on-demand + 10%).
4) SLO credit: if SLO compliance falls below threshold, apply credit equal to X% of the committed charge for the affected period (formula: committed_charge * max(0, (target_compliance - observed_compliance) / target_compliance) * SLA_factor).

Console and telemetry changes (UX notes):
- New Console page: "Fractional Capacity" under Billing & Capacity. Views: active bundles, SLO health heatmap, fallback counts, projected month-end consumption delta.
- Alerts: default alert if observed compliance < target by 0.5% for 12h. Owners: customer-success + infra-oncall.

Rollout & migration plan (recommended):
1) Pilot: Q2 2027 — small set of mid-market beta customers on Hosted with manual provisioning and heavy SE support.
2) Automation: Q3 2027 — full self-serve sign-up, Console UX, and automated capacity ledger integration.
3) Dedicated support: Q4 2027 — map fractional units to dedicated partitions and allow migration.
4) General availability: targeted for early 2028 after 3 months of adoption metrics and reliability KPIs.

Migration guidelines for existing customers:
- For customers on per-token: offer a conversion tool to estimate monthly committed units from historical 90-day usage and target SLO, with recommended initial bundle and a 30-day evaluation term.
- For Dedicated customers: allow conversion of a subset of reserved racks into fractional units for internal chargeback and new product lines.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Commercial: conversion rate from self-serve to fractional bundles, ARR from fractional products, average committed unit size.
- Reliability: SLO compliance >= 99.5% for pilot group, fallback rates < 5% of requests.
- Financial: realized ASP vs forecast within ±8%, overage revenue within forecast caps.
